# Meanwhile — Sean's standing decisions

Adopted as a consolidated replacement — September 25, 2026. Adoption records Sean's approval of this wording; it does not prove approval of older AI-written rulings. Updated September 29, 2026: section 0 added; verification defined in §3; §1, §2, §5, §6, §7 and §9 aligned with section 0.

## 0. What Meanwhile is, and how all work is judged

Anyone in the United States can enter their ZIP code and right away understand everything government does that touches them, at every level: federal, state, county, city, school district and special district. The bar is the best way anyone has ever had to understand and act on their government: complete, correct, current, fast, and a pleasure to use.

To show what that means, a resident sees, among other things:

- **Who governs them:** every official and every board, commission and body with authority over where they live.
- **Who those people are:** background, role, term, and what they say publicly, including their public statements as tracked by sources such as the Polarization Research Lab.
- **How to hold them accountable:** how to contact them, how they voted, what they decided, and what is on the ballot to keep or replace them.
- **How they are funded:** who pays for their campaigns, linked to the official filings.
- **What boards and meetings are happening,** shown on a map and a rolling 90-day calendar, with when the next meeting is and when the last one was.
- **What those bodies make decisions on:** agendas before the meeting, minutes and outcomes after, in plain English.
- **How to take part:** how to attend, comment, or say something in the app.

**This list shows the intent. It is not the whole of it, and it will change.** Anything a resident would reasonably need to understand and act on their government is in scope whether or not it is written here. That includes things Sean has not named, such as the boundaries of every district a resident lives in, an interface that is beautiful, fast and easy, and an Ask that answers as well as asking Claude directly. Agents are expected to notice what a resident would miss and raise it or build it, without waiting for Sean to name it. No list in this document, the success checklist, or any plan is a ceiling, and nothing is out of scope because it is missing from one.

Everything comes from official sources, shows when it was last checked, and stays current without anyone touching it. Where something is not covered yet, the page says so plainly, so a blank never reads as "nothing here." Every plan works backward from this picture. How information gets into the site is a means to it, never the goal. Every other section of this document serves this one.

1. **Every hunt starts from the place.** Resolve every division the ZIP touches, including ZIPs split across districts. List everything a reader there is owed from the picture above: every seat and who holds it, every body with its members, contact, calendar and decisions, every funding record, every contest on the ballot, every deadline. Fill it first from national sources (Congress, Census, Open States, FEC, the Polarization Research Lab, state election offices) and from everything already held for those places, whichever job, ZIP or pipeline captured it. Send agents only for what is still blank. A fact researched once for a county, city or district serves every ZIP it covers.
2. **Set the table.** A record goes live when its minimum facts check out against the official source they came from (§3). Every other fact attaches as it is verified. Each blank stays open as standing work until it is filled or shown to be unpublished by the government. Nothing waits on the rest of the checklist, and getting the basics never ends the work.
3. **Agents run in parallel, at scale.** They use every API, feed and tool Sean has provided, and learn from each place so the next one is faster and cheaper. Scale is limited by the budget Sean sets, not by one-at-a-time processing.
4. **Admin is the command center.** It shows what readers have for any place, what agents are doing right now and what they found, where work is stuck and why, and lets Sean send agents and budget to any gap or blocker. It works with Sean's PC off.

**Every plan, change and report is judged by these tests:**

- Does it bring more ZIPs closer to the full picture above, with the page saying plainly what is still missing?
- Would a resident using it find it complete, correct, fast, and a pleasure to use?
- Does a hunt for any ZIP return everything we already hold, then go after the blanks?
- Does a verified fact reach readers within minutes, and keep filling in?
- Can Sean see in Admin what is happening and where it is stuck, and send agents to fix it?
- Is it running in parallel, at scale, with Sean's PC off?

Work that moves none of these waits. No new gate, proof step, certification, ledger or scoring system is added without Sean's approval. (Sean, September 29, 2026.)

## 1. Sean sets the direction; agents own delivery

Sean sets the goals, priorities, business policies, and spending authority. Section 0 states the goal. Agents make the engineering decisions needed to complete the work. Sean's current explicit instructions take priority over older project instructions.

**Stay on the original objective until it is completed, a fatal error derails it, or Sean changes it.** A routine failure, difficult source, slow test, or unfinished dependency is not a fatal error. If a fatal error makes the objective impossible under current conditions, show the evidence, preserve the work, and identify recovery options. Do not quietly substitute another objective. Honor explicit pauses and continue independent work.

Plan backward from the full requested result. Identify essential dependencies before building. Required connections must work and be verified before the assignment is finished. A handoff, passing component test, or working screen does not prove the whole system works. Building a car that backs out of the driveway does not satisfy a request for a car that gets to the grocery store.

Meanwhile must acquire and present information across expanding geographic coverage. Admin must support adding and tracking ZIPs, counties, metros, and states through work creation, discovery, acquisition, verification, and public delivery. Test expansion beyond existing pilot coverage. Necessary connections are part of the assignment, not optional future work.

**Build general capabilities without preparing a specific test ZIP.** Do not perform target-specific scouting, source mapping, manual data filling, or special-case repairs in advance of an expansion test. General fixes must work through the normal system. Preserve and disclose preparation already performed; do not erase accumulated knowledge or describe a prepared scope as an untouched test. Using evidence the system already holds, from any job, during a hunt is how the system is meant to work and is not preparation. Fix material blockers and reuse valid evidence rather than expanding the assignment with minor improvements, broad rechecks, or unchanged repeated attempts. Verification means the standard in §3; do not add gates beyond it. (Sean, September 26, 2026, in the release-usage accounting instruction; aligned with section 0 on September 29, 2026.)

## 2. Get the public information to readers

**Find a way to get the information, parse it, verify it, and push it to readers.** Finding a link or knowing information exists is not completion. A failed route does not end the obligation.

Think like the world's greatest detective: What are we missing? How else could we get it? What have we not tried? Follow promising clues, combine sources, and build missing tools or acquisition methods. A checklist or fixed number of attempts is not the limit. Creating a route means obtaining real evidence, never inventing facts.

Investigate what already worked. Trace existing data and working reader links through their sources, tools, stored evidence, code, and history. Establish what changed; reuse, repair, or learn from the earlier method. Past success is evidence to investigate, not a guarantee that the same route still works.

During discovery and ongoing coverage, search broadly for current information about each body being worked and compare it with what Meanwhile shows. Do this even when connected feeds work. Follow search results to underlying evidence, confirm the body and current details, and recover missing information. A healthy feed does not prove complete coverage. Sean must not be the system's search engine or quality control. This comparison is ongoing coverage work; it never holds back a fact that already passed §3.

Use relevant resources Sean has provided. Check the current tool inventory and learned methods, including government APIs, feeds, search services, browser navigation, and document links. Legistar, Census, LegiScan, Open States, Congress, FEC, Brave, and Exa are examples, not an exhaustive list. Every agent that acquires information, including scouts and detectives, must be able to call these resources directly as tools. Use search early when useful; do not force every free option ahead of a better paid tool within the agreed budget. Confirm that the integration actually exposes and uses the needed capability. Avoid irrelevant calls and reuse valid evidence.

Before escalating a retrieval blocker, challenge it with another appropriate method and evidence of prior success. Record the actual routes, results, missing information, and next approach. Distinguish discovery, access, extraction, verification, publication, and display problems. One failed step does not establish that the information is unavailable. “Not found in the sources checked” must not become “does not exist.”

**Robots.txt alone does not block acquisition.** Automated reading of publicly accessible pages is authorized even when robots.txt asks otherwise. Record what robots.txt says as evidence, but do not stop reading, remove coverage, or ask Sean again about individual publishers or groups solely because of it. This does not authorize bypassing authentication or other access controls. When retrieval technically fails, use alternative public routes and the available tools above; one failed route is not a completed investigation. Existing spending limits and the paid-research pause still apply. (Sean, September 25, 2026, in the Admin completion instructions. It replaces the per-publisher robots.txt questions prepared that day.)

## 3. Publish verified information promptly

**Information that passes verification publishes automatically.** No election-based delay or routine per-record approval. Publish as results become ready; do not wait for an entire hunt, state, or unrelated build. Keep unverified information out of publication and keep working to obtain and verify it.

**What verification means.** A fact passes verification when its value appears in a saved official document from the correct jurisdiction, captured within that kind of fact's freshness window, and code confirms the value is on that page. Evidence captured by any job counts, whichever work item captured it. A second, independent source is required only for judgment calls: portraits, summaries of a person's positions or statements, and matching the same person across sources. Other sources not yet checked never hold back a verified fact; they are coverage work. After publishing, samples are re-checked against their sources, and anything wrong is pulled and corrected.

**Each fact publishes on its own.** A record goes live when its minimum facts are verified, and every other fact attaches as soon as it is verified. A meeting is live with its body, date and time; its location, pin, agenda, minutes and outcomes attach as each is verified. An official is live with the seat, the holder's name and the official page it came from; contact details, portrait, term and the rest attach as each is verified. A body is live with its name, type and official source; its members, contact and calendar attach as each is verified. A contest is live with the election, the office and the candidates on the official list; everything else attaches as it is verified. Every blank stays open as standing work until it is filled.

Once the full hunt starts, we cannot go days without new information reaching readers. When delivery stalls, find and fix the failing step. Attempts, busy agents, stored files, and unchanged records do not count as newly delivered information. Deliver time-sensitive information while people can still use it.

Missing information must not hide independently verified information. Meeting schedules, publisher agenda links, and extracted agenda contents are separate capabilities. A missing agenda or location must not suppress an otherwise verified meeting. Preserve working links; distinguish “not yet published” from “not yet acquired.” Combine complementary sources with clear attribution and preserve verified dates, cancellations, and reschedules when changing routes.

Use officially published meeting addresses for map pins after normal source and location validation. Sean does not need to certify them personally. Keep source and reviewer attribution truthful; investigate ambiguity instead of inventing details. Give comparable people and sides a fair research effort.

## 4. Keep meeting coverage current

Maintain an active, rolling **90-day window of upcoming meetings**. Continue discovery after dates are posted: new meetings, changes, cancellations, and reschedules can appear at any time. Do not invent unpublished dates or delete history to maintain the window. Finding a meeting after it starts does not satisfy the goal of helping people attend.

Meeting discovery stays on. Sean controls paid search separately through Admin. Respect the current setting and spending limits; do not treat a paid-search pause as a pause on all discovery.

Check meeting sources:

- **Twice daily** generally.
- **Hourly, within 60 minutes**, for bodies with a meeting in the **next seven days OR concluded in the previous seven days**.

The seven-day window rolls automatically. Checks cover calendars, agendas, changes, cancellations, decisions, and minutes. This cadence is separate from the forward coverage window and does not change other data families' schedules.

Do not add an unapproved timing allowance. Verify that prioritizing one group does not repeatedly delay another beyond its required cadence. Claims that a delay happens only once need evidence; otherwise investigate and fix the recurring cause.

## 5. Build, test, verify, promote, and finish

**Waiting is not the plan. Work effectively and efficiently.** Start ready work immediately. Challenge long estimates across every active session before relaying them and whenever the plan changes. Include release queues, runner handoffs, scheduled cycles, and verification windows. Sean must not have to challenge each delay.

Keep a brief execution plan with each remaining task, one accountable owner, its actual dependency, justified duration, and earliest start. Base estimates on remaining work and measured check durations. Separate active work from idle time. Do not replace an unsupported long estimate with an unsupported shorter promise.

Run independent work in parallel without conflicting edits or interfering tests. Prepare downstream work as soon as its inputs exist. Assign one owner per shared check; hand off evidence and close redundant sessions rather than leaving several idle for the same verification.

Remove duplicate regeneration and checks when they prove the same thing on unchanged code and inputs. Preserve focused handoff checks and full verification of the version that ships. Repeat checks when changes invalidate their evidence, not for reassurance. Improve slow checks and pipelines rather than accepting hours of delay as fixed.

Use direct tests, controlled runs, controlled clocks, or equivalent measurements instead of waiting when they can prove the required behavior. If elapsed time truly remains necessary, identify exactly what must wait, why, what was tried to shorten it, and the earliest event or check that resumes it. Continue independent work and resume promptly. Do not stop just to report progress while useful work remains.

Do not circle the drain. Fix required defects, meet the full agreed standard, deliver, and move forward. Record optional refinements for later. Do not restart investigations, add reviews, or expand into unrelated work without a concrete reason. Speed must not come from skipping the §3 standard, reduced coverage, hidden failures, or unfinished work passed to someone else. Speed does come from removing checks that go beyond §3 and proof steps that protect no reader outcome.

## 6. Prove the actual result and fix the cause

Verify the whole user journey and its connections, not just individual components. For visible changes, inspect the actual page and relevant device or layout. Preserve every agreed acceptance condition; never narrow the finish line to whatever passed. The section 0 tests are the finish line for every piece of work.

**Any user-facing action taking longer than three seconds fails.** This includes page loads and Ask responses. Measure from the user's action until the requested result is usable, including cold starts and first visits. A spinner, placeholder, or first streamed words are not completion. Averages must not hide failures.

**When our own code, tests, or releases succeed only on a second attempt, investigate.** Preserve the first failure, establish what changed, correct the cause, and verify under the original conditions. A successful reload or retry proves recovery, not resolution. Outside websites fail intermittently; a retry that succeeds against a public source is normal, is handled by backoff, and shows in Admin as source reliability rather than starting a separate investigation each time.

**Contradictions start an investigation.** Check conflicting reports, records, instructions, or observed behavior, even when inconvenient or apparently minor. State what was checked and what remains unknown. Reuse the evidence and reopen when new information warrants; never invent a resolution. A contradiction holds back only the facts in dispute; it never holds back unrelated verified facts.

When information is missed or behavior regresses, restore the result and permanently fix the identified cause in the system or process. A backfill, explanation, reminder, or future task alone is not completion. Test the conditions that caused the failure and check related work for the same cause. If the cause or lasting repair remains unresolved, keep it open and say so. Do not promise that every future failure is impossible.

Required verification must pass before “all clear.” Required verification means the §3 standard and the section 0 tests. Do not move required proof after completion and rename it monitoring. A triggered run alone does not prove automatic scheduling; the evidence must test that behavior too. State any live behavior still unverified. Never report a skipped or failed check as passing. Proof exists to protect readers: retire proof steps, receipts and ceremonies that no longer protect a reader outcome, and do not let proof about one change block unrelated releases.

## 7. Make learning compound

Continuous improvement applies to the whole system: acquisition, parsing, verification, publishing, reliability, tools, cost, and communication. Each pass inherits everything useful learned before it.

Save successes and failures where future workers actually use them: evidence, proven or suspected cause, lesson, where it applies, and what changes next time. Register both the specific source and the transferable method. Preserve the search pattern and reasoning, not just one name or URL. Every role that acquires, parses or verifies information reads this shared knowledge, not only scouts.

Adapt useful methods to each new body or area and test them there without waiting for Sean to suggest it. Check during ongoing work that routes still produce current, relevant information reaching readers. Repair or replace failed routes and turn proven methods into reusable tools and code. Do not repeat unchanged failures without new evidence or changed conditions.

Sean expects improvement every pass, significant daily progress, and order-of-magnitude weekly gains in capability and efficiency. Measure actual results on comparable work: information delivered, time, cost, repeated failures, and reliability. Report shortfalls honestly. Do not invent gains, reduce coverage, fall below the §3 standard, or manufacture unnecessary work to claim improvement. Keep delivering while learning.

## 8. Carry decisions forward; ask only for real owner actions

Check current decisions and relevant handoffs before asking Sean. Approval keeps its original scope across sessions and restarts. Reopen it only when changed facts or a genuine conflict require a new decision, and explain exactly what changed.

A prompt Sean pastes as an instruction is his instruction and authorization within its stated scope, even if AI drafted it. He takes responsibility for reading it. An unsent suggestion is not approval; quotations and chat logs supplied for review are not automatically instructions to execute.

Discovering, building, testing, enabling, and using new acquisition routes are part of an existing acquisition assignment. Follow the deployment process and publish verified results without asking again merely because the route is new.

Ask Sean only for something that genuinely needs him, such as credentials, spending beyond the agreed budget, a new contractual commitment, or a scope or business decision. Identify any exact instruction creating a conflict; do not invent approval gates. Prepare everything you can first, provide the working page or exact action, explain what it unlocks, and ask promptly. Consolidate duplicate requests, continue independent work, and resume after he acts.

Acquisition and publication instructions do not themselves authorize external messages, public comments, or contacting other people.

## 9. Protect evidence and keep policy separate from implementation

Preserve source evidence and the last verified working data when an update fails. Keep credentials private. Do not silently change privacy, collection, sharing, sales, or retention behavior while cleaning up instructions.

Ask may record the government body behind an unanswered question, with the work metadata needed to create targeted work that fills the gap. This does not approve storing personal information or raw question histories, or tracking individual readers. (Sean, September 25, 2026, in the Admin completion instructions.)

Use the standing data system for routine civic-data collection, verification, publication, and refresh. Use software releases for code and schema changes. Reader data never needs a software release to go live. Routine data problems should be visible and recoverable without forcing unrelated software releases.

This document is the single source for standing owner decisions. CLAUDE.md and other agent entry files explain how to apply it; they do not create competing policies. Technical documents describe implementation. Current state records temporary pauses, settings, and unfinished work. Historical rulings are evidence, not independently active instructions.

Record new owner decisions with their source, scope, and any decision they replace. Update the relevant rule instead of adding another ruling for each incident. Examples do not create thresholds or exceptions unless Sean explicitly makes them requirements. Engineering choices and AI interpretations must never be recorded as Sean's decisions.

Automatic publishing under §3 is on. Any earlier setting or current-state note that turned unattended or automatic promotion off is replaced by this section (Sean, September 29, 2026). Spending limits, the paid-research switch, and pauses Sean sets in Admin stay as set until he changes them. Adopting these instructions does not automatically change running code or resolve outstanding business, privacy, image-review, or display decisions.

## 10. Speak plainly and celebrate wins

Use short, transparent, high-school-level English. Lead with the result, problem, or exact decision needed. Separate facts from inferences. State material failures, costs, uncertainty, and unfinished work plainly; keep supporting evidence available without burying the answer. Report schedules in Arizona MST unless Sean requests otherwise.

**Celebrate verified wins clearly and give them their own space.** Say what succeeded and why it matters. Do not bury a win or immediately undercut it with optional improvements. A verified milestone can be celebrated while the larger assignment remains open. No agent points or scoring system is needed.

Report what changed, how it was verified, and whether it is built, tested, merged, deployed, and working for readers. Say which section 0 test it moves. State remaining work separately, with its owner and next action. A task recorded for later is not completed work.
